landings.summary: How Indian founders form a mainland or free zone company in Dubai: licence type, ownership, documents from India and the steps after the licence.
landings.contentHtml:
What company formation means for an Indian owner

Indian entrepreneurs, trading companies and professionals are among the largest groups setting up in Dubai, helped by close trade ties and the India-UAE trade agreement in force since 2022. The Indian government told Parliament in 2023 that about 3.5 million Indians live in the UAE. This page explains how the Dubai side of company formation works when the owners, directors or shareholders are based in India, and where your home country adds extra steps. The full service is described in our guide to company formation and business setup, and the country overview is in setting up in Dubai from India.

Mainland or free zone for owners in India

A mainland licence from the Department of Economy and Tourism lets the company trade across the UAE and rent premises in the city. A free zone licence is issued by the zone's own authority and often suits companies that serve customers outside the UAE. If your customers are mostly in India or other export markets, compare both before you choose; our DED and DET services page explains how the licence types differ.

Home-country points that affect this service

  • Indian residents are generally taxed on worldwide income, and overseas investment by residents is governed by Reserve Bank of India and foreign exchange rules. India and the UAE have a double tax avoidance agreement. Confirm the structure with an Indian tax adviser before you invest.
  • Indian residents can remit funds abroad only within the limits and purposes that foreign exchange rules allow, and overseas direct investment has its own conditions. Use your authorised bank and keep the paperwork for every transfer.
  • India is a party to the Apostille Convention, and the Ministry of External Affairs and state authorities handle attestation and apostille of Indian documents. Documents usually need notarisation or attestation by the issuing authority first, and an Arabic translation for UAE use.

Documents and information to prepare

  • Passport copies of every shareholder and manager (valid for at least six months is a common requirement)
  • Proof of address in India, such as a recent bank letter or utility bill, where the authority asks for it
  • For a corporate shareholder: certificate of incorporation, articles and a board resolution from India, attested for UAE use
  • Memorandum of Association, signed in Dubai or in front of a notary abroad with the correct attestation
  • Proposed trade name and a plain-language description of the activity

How it works from India

  1. Confirm the activity, ownership and number of visas, and choose mainland or a free zone.
  2. Sign the memorandum and any power of attorney, and attest documents from India (POA drafting, MOA drafting).
  3. Obtain initial approval, register the tenancy and submit the licence application.
  4. After the licence: corporate tax registration, residence files (visa support) and bank account documents.

Currency and payments

The dirham is pegged to the US dollar, so the rupee-dirham rate follows the rupee-dollar market. Ask your bank which rate and fees it applies to outward transfers.

  • Document Clearing for Indian clients: read the India guide

Documents usually need notarisation or attestation by the issuing authority first, and an Arabic translation for UAE use.

faqs.question: How long does company formation take for owners in India?

faqs.answer: Start with the UAE Government Portal (u.ae) and Invest in Dubai for licensing and the Federal Tax Authority for corporate tax. For rules in India, check the Reserve Bank of India and an Indian tax adviser.
